issue.body:
# Bug report

### Bug description:

```python
import unittest
from xml.parsers import expat
class SetAttributeTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.parser = expat.ParserCreate(namespace_separator='!')
data = b'<?xml version="1.0" encoding="iso-8859-1" standalone="no"?>\n<?xml-stylesheet href="stylesheet.css"?>\n<!-- comment data -->\n<!DOCTYPE quotations SYSTEM "quotations.dtd" [\n<!ELEMENT root ANY>\n<!ATTLIST root attr1 CDATA #REQUIRED attr2 CDATA #IMPLIED>\n<!NOTATION notation SYSTEM "notation.jpeg">\n<!ENTITY acirc "â">\n<!ENTITY external_entity SYSTEM "entity.file">\n<!ENTITY unparsed_entity SYSTEM "entity.file" NDATA notation>\n%unparsed_entity;\n]>\n\n<root attr1="value1" attr2="value2ὀ">\n<myns:subelement xmlns:myns="http://www.python.org/namespace">\n     Contents of subelements\n</myns:subelement>\n<sub2><![CDATA[contents of CDATA section]]></sub2>\n&external_entity;\n&skipped_entity;\n\xb5\n</root>\n'
class ParseTest(unittest.TestCase):
    class Outputter:
        def __init__(self):
            self.out = []
        def NotStandaloneHandler(self):
            return 3.1415926535897932384626
        def ExternalEntityRefHandler(self, *args):
            return 1
        def XmlDeclHandler(self, *args):
            return 1
        def ElementDeclHandler(self, *args):
            return 1
    handler_names = ['NotStandaloneHandler', 'ExternalEntityRefHandler', 'XmlDeclHandler', 'ElementDeclHandler']
    def _hookup_callbacks(self, parser, handler):
        for name in self.handler_names:
            setattr(parser, name, getattr(handler, name))
    def test_parse_str(self):
        out = self.Outputter()
        parser = expat.ParserCreate(namespace_separator='!')
        self._hookup_callbacks(parser, out)
        parser.Parse(data.decode('iso-8859-1'), True)
if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
```

comments.body:
This is in vendored code from what I gather from a quick look, please report it [upstream](https://github.com/libexpat/libexpat).

CC @hartwork

Hi!

> This is in vendored code from what I gather from a quick look, please report it [upstream](https://github.com/libexpat/libexpat).

@StanFromIreland it ~will~ would need a reproducer in C for upstream.

Let me try to throw this at ASan-enabled CPython myself and see if I can reproduce it and how much it can be cut down. Starting…
@StanFromIreland I think I got it, it seems to be a bug in CPython, not upstream Expat. Details and a pull request upcoming…

@StanFromIreland I confirm that branch `main` — commit d74a96366df58b6e55d4a03612c3e67da2211ddd for me — is affected and that the reproducer can be cut down to this:

```python
import unittest
from xml.parsers import expat
from textwrap import dedent

data = dedent('''\
    <!DOCTYPE quotations SYSTEM "quotations.dtd" [
        <!ELEMENT root ANY>
    ]>
    <root/>
''').encode('UTF-8')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    parser = expat.ParserCreate()
    parser.NotStandaloneHandler = lambda: 1.234  # arbitrary float
    parser.ElementDeclHandler = lambda _1, _2: None
    parser.Parse(data, True)
```

@YuanchengJiang for the next bug you report, please provide a minimal reproducer from the beginning — thanks!

It should be noted that `NotStandaloneHandler` returning a `float` crashes like this at runtime, followed by the LeakSanitizer output:

```console
# ./python leak.py 
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "[..]/cpython/leak.py", line 17, in <module>
    parser.Parse(data, True)
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^
TypeError: 'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer

=================================================================
==27024==ERROR: LeakSanitizer: detected memory leaks

Direct leak of 56 byte(s) in 1 object(s) allocated from:
[..]
    #6 0x7bdbc561bffe in doProlog Modules/expat/xmlparse.c:6096
[..]

SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: 56 byte(s) leaked in 1 allocation(s).
```

For me it's 56 bytes rather than 32 but it's the same code location — the code at `xmlparse.c:6096` is this:

https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/d74a96366df58b6e55d4a03612c3e67da2211ddd/Modules/expat/xmlparse.c#L6096

libexpat allocates the content model there and it must be freed by a call to [`XML_FreeContentModel`](https://libexpat.github.io/doc/api/latest/#XML_FreeContentModel) by the element declaration handler when one is registered as with our case. The CPython code at…

https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/d74a96366df58b6e55d4a03612c3e67da2211ddd/Modules/pyexpat.c#L675-L678

…in function `my_ElementDeclHandler` does that — good! —, but there is one exit path in the function that bypasses this clean-up, here:

https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/d74a96366df58b6e55d4a03612c3e67da2211ddd/Modules/pyexpat.c#L644-L645

Once I turn that `return` into `goto finally;` the leak disappears. Pull request #140602 fixes that issue and is ready for review :beers:
@hartwork thanks. I have tried to debloat the PoC before reporting, however, it might not be the minimized one.
Thank you @YuanchengJiang for the report and @hartwork for the fix! (and backports)
So, we can close this issue?
Yes, we can close issues once backports are merged. I don't consider this a security issue so no need for security patches.
